title: Root Knot Nematodes in Vegetables - Nepal

Header: Root Knot Nematodes in Vegetables - Nepal
Meloidogyne incognita, M. javanica, M. arenaria, M. hapla तरकारीबालीकोजरामागाँठा बनाउनेजुकाह ᱧ

Prevention: Choose a field without a history of root-knot nematodes.
Flood the field for 1-3 weeks before planting wherever possible.
Follow crop rotation with cereal crops (e.g. rice, maize, wheat, etc) for at least 2 years.
Use disease-free seedlings raised in solarised soil, virgin soil or peat moss.
Use tomato seedlings grafted with root-knot resistant wild brinjals, Solanum sisymbriifolium or
Apply mustard cake @ 250-300g per 1m2 at the time of field preparation.
Apply crushed yellow mustard seed @ 20g per planting hole at the time of transplanting.
Burn the root-knot infected roots after harvesting the crop.
Maintain field sanitation by removing soil particles from farm appliances by proper washing.
Monitoring: Observe the plant/field on weekly basis for yellow patches, stunted growth or wilting.
Observe galls on the root system.
Send soil samples to a lab to test for the presence of nematodes.
Direct Control: Uproot infected plants having big galls on main root and destroy them e.g. by burning them.
If the galls are smaller and limited to adventitious roots, apply mustard cake @ 40g per plant to soil by slightly digging and mixing within a ring of 5cm around the plant.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label.
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance.
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB).
